Today if `checkAndListenPldmService` throws, we catch in BiosHandler constructor and log a PEL. With your change, `checkAndListenPldmService` exceptions are caught locally and trace is logged, and no PEL is logged. So the error path has changed. Is this alright?
Yes that is fine.
why is try catch retained?
Worst case "std::make_shared" can throw.
Acknowledged
`noexcept` specifier missing
Acknowledged, marked in header file.
Log a PEL here ?

Eventually moving away from PELs in the service load phase due to performance, hence did not add it here.
All these logs will be captured as a part of new logging class going forward, hence will be retained.
Acknowledged
Should have a `nullptr` check on `biosHandler`.
Acknowledged
why do we need the nullptr check ?
If std::make_shared in the constructor throws, this will be a nullPtr.
throw will to the catch and not continue. as we have std::make_shared in many places without the check , just the try catch.

> If std::make_shared in the constructor throws, this will be a nullPtr.

I was referring to why we have try/catch in the bios handler constructor but even in that case, the pointer here won't be null. so better have try/catch here and not in the constructor is what I am assuming.
Acknowledged

If the `std::make_shared<>` at Line 245 in `bios_handler.hpp` throws exception, `m_specificBiosHandler` will be `nullptr`.  We should have a `nullptr` check here.

`m_specificBiosHandler` is also being used inside `listenBiosAttributes()`, so should have a check there as well.

The error handling has been moved to manager main.cpp.
Hence we will not hit this path.
Done
LGTM
We should add a `@throw` section here?

Does that actually impacts? It holds value if there is an impact.
